scenes.heading: Data Sharing & Marketplaces
scenes.narration: Modern warehouses let you share live data across accounts and organizations without ever copying or moving it.

scenes.heading: How modern sharing works
bullets: Shares grant read access to your data, not a physical copy.
Consumers query your live data using their own compute.
There is no ETL, no pipelines, and no stale duplicates.
Marketplaces let providers publish datasets for many consumers.
scenes.narration: Instead of exporting files, you create a share that grants read access to selected objects. Consumers query that live data with their own warehouses, so they pay for their own compute. Because nothing is copied, everyone always sees the latest data with no pipelines to maintain.

scenes.heading: The sharing workflow
scenes.narration: The provider creates a share and grants specific tables or views to it. They then add a consumer account, which mounts the share as a read-only database. From there the consumer queries the provider's live data instantly, using their own compute resources.

scenes.heading: Copy-based vs live sharing
scenes.narration: Traditional sharing exports files that are stale the moment they are sent and require pipelines to keep flowing. Live secure sharing grants governed read access to the same underlying storage, so data is never duplicated. Access is always current and can be revoked instantly, which is far safer and simpler.

scenes.heading: Creating a secure share
scenes.narration: The provider creates a share and grants usage on the database along with select on the specific table. Adding the partner account gives them read access to that live data. The consumer never receives a copy; they simply query the provider's storage directly through their own warehouse.

scenes.text: Secure data sharing grants live, zero-copy access, and marketplaces scale that into a whole ecosystem of datasets.
scenes.narration: Live sharing replaces brittle exports with instant, governed access, and marketplaces turn that into an entire data ecosystem.
